subject: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@finex.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models

Hi Susan — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we covered and the next steps we discussed: 

Pain points we heard
- Primary cost driver: ~ $18k/mo on OpenAI usage for both chat and embeddings.
- Latency: occasional tail latency spikes (p95/p99) impacting user experience for real-time chat.
- Vendor lock-in concerns: proprietary API feature reliance (function-calling, streaming, embeddings) that would be costly to re-engineer.
- Data/privacy: need to avoid sending certain PII to third-party managed endpoints; interested in Private/Dedicated deployment options.

Current stack
- Chat + function-calling: OpenAI (gpt-4o/gpt-4.1) and some Anthropic usage for assistant flows.
- Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-003 (1536-dim) powering document retrieval.
- Orchestration: LangChain-based microservices on GCP; model calls are wrapped behind an API layer.

Success criteria for migration
- No regression in answer quality and function-calling behavior for 80%+ of highest-value prompts.
- Embedding parity (similar recall for top-5 retrievals) with minimal tuning.
- Latency within current SLOs (p50 < 120ms for small prompts, p95 within acceptable range).
- Cost reduction target: ~40% lower inference spend (token + compute) at steady state.
- Deployment options: hosted short-term for PoC, Dedicated/Private for production with KMS and audit logs.

Compatibility needs
- Function-calling and structured JSON outputs.
- Streaming responses for chat.
- Embedding dimension compatibility (1536) or clear migration path.
- API compatibility to minimize engineering changes (OpenAI-compatible endpoint is helpful).

Suggested model shortlist (initial candidates for PoC)
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (quantized variant) — good cost/latency profile for assistant flows.
- Llama-2-13B-chat (int8/qat) — stronger instruction-following, good for function-calling parity.
- RedPajama-INCITE-13B or similar open instruct variants for closed-domain fine-tuning.
- For embeddings: open-embed-1536-equivalent models (we can evaluate embedding parity).

Next steps (proposed)
1) Redwood sets up a 2-week PoC: benchmarking (latency, throughput), embedding parity tests, and quality evals against your sample prompts.
2) Technical deep-dive (30-45m) with Rishi to align on infra, authentication, and test data.
3) Share SOC2 and compliance docs (attached).
4) Pricing estimate and Dedicated/Private sizing after baseline runs.

Attachments: redwood_poc_scope.pdf (PoC scope), soc2_summary.pdf (compliance summary), model_shortlist_comparison.csv (high-level perf/cost estimates).

Please reply with confirmation of the priorities above and any additional constraints (e.g., retention/purge policies, country-specific data residency). I can schedule the technical deep-dive for early next week if that works.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and matches our notes. A few clarifications / additional context: 

- Monthly spend on OpenAI calls is closer to $18k-$22k depending on growth month; embeddings are ~40% of that.
- We rely heavily on OpenAI function-calling for structured actions (payment lookups, account fetches) and it's critical we preserve the function schema behavior.
- Embedding dimension is 1536 — we need a drop-in or a migration plan that preserves our retrieval accuracy.
- We use streaming to show progressive chat responses in the UI; p50/p90 are acceptable today but p99 spikes cause UX issues.

We're keen on a PoC. Can you confirm the sandbox access model (do you need API keys or can Redwood provide a private test instance)? Also, are you able to include an initial cost comparison for Mistral-7B vs Llama-2-13B for both chat and embeddings?

We're available for a technical deep-dive on Tue 6/23 or Wed 6/24 in the morning (PDT).

Thanks,
Susan Park

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models

Thanks for the quick reply, Susan — confirmed on your priorities. A few quick answers and proposed schedule: 

Sandbox / PoC access
- For the PoC we can do one of two things depending on your security preference:
  1) Hosted PoC: Redwood provides a scoped test environment in our hosted API with truncated data retention and explicit logging controls (fastest to start).
  2) Dedicated sandbox: a short-lived Dedicated pool in your VPC (requires a little more setup but mirrors production).

Initial cost comparison (high level)
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (quantized): expected compute cost ~35-50% lower than current OpenAI spend for chat for equivalent throughput.
- Llama-2-13B-chat (int8): slightly higher compute than Mistral but better for complex instruction-following and function-calling parity; cost vs quality trade-off.
- Embeddings: we will benchmark a 1536-dim open embedding candidate; in many cases you can get comparable retrieval with fine-tuning or a small embedding model for ~20-30% lower cost.

Proposed timeline
- Week 0: kickoff + test data transfer (you share sanitized sample prompts + representative docs).
- Week 1: performance/compatibility runs (latency, streaming, function-calling tests).
- Week 2: embedding parity evaluation + quality review and cost estimate.

I've attached the PoC scope and our SOC2 summary. If that looks good, I'll lock in Tue 6/23 9:30am PDT for the technical deep-dive with Rishi.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models (technical)

Hi Susan — looping in on the technical thread. A few practical asks so we can scope and run the PoC efficiently: 

1) Can you share a small set (50-200) of representative prompts and a ~1k doc sample for embedding parity tests? Prefer sanitized data or a synthetic equivalent if you have PII concerns.
2) If you can provide a short list of the function schemas you use today (example JSONs) that will help us validate function-calling parity.
3) For the streaming check we'll need a couple of long prompts and the UX behavior you expect (chunking strategy).
4) If you prefer Hosted PoC, we'll issue scoped API keys with retention controls. For Dedicated sandbox we'll schedule a quick network kickoff.

Deliverables from Redwood after PoC:
- Latency and throughput baselines for each model candidate
- Embedding recall/precision comparison (top-5 retrieval)
- Function-calling compatibility report with remediation guidance
- Estimated cost per 100k requests for chosen model(s)

Please drop the sample artifacts to the Drive link Marissa shared or reply to this thread and I'll create a secure upload. Looking forward to the deep-dive on 6/23 9:30am PDT.
